The views and opinions of authors expressed herein do not necessarily state or reflect those of the United States Government or any agency thereof.” DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT Executive Summary ION Clean Energy® (ION) is deploying its transformational solvent-based CO capture technology 2 as part of the effort to decarbonize the electrical grid. In preparation for a full-scale commercial deployment of ION’s solvent technology, ION has partnered with Calpine, Koch Modular Process Systems (KMPS), and Sargent & Lundy (S&L) to design, construct and commission a 1 MWe CO 2 capture pilot plant at Calpine’s Los Medanos Energy Center (LMEC), a commercially-dispatched natural gas combined cycle (NGCC) power plant, in Pittsburg, CA. ION generated design documents for the construction team and incorporated KMPS’s engineering expertise to produce a Process Design Package that formed the basis for a Preliminary Design Review and HAZOP meetings. S&L designed the balance of plant (BOP) and collaborated with Calpine to deliver utilities to the pilot. KMPS oversaw the fabrication and delivery of the modules whereby S&L was responsible for the final module installation and connections to the host site and BOP. ION performed final commissioning and initial startup of the unit in September 2023. This pilot, known as Project Enterprise (ENTP), was intended to allow ION to further demonstrate the capabilities and superior stability of its carbon capture solvents and to provide key learnings in preparation for the design, construction, and operation of a full-scale commercial CO capture 2 facility. After successful commissioning of the pilot system, the initial phase of the pilot testing consisted of baselining the system using aqueous monoethanolamine (MEA) at 30 wt%, an industry standard carbon capture solvent. Operating with MEA allowed ION to create a baseline to compare the performance of ION’s proprietary solvents. ION operated the ENTP pilot with MEA for approximately 250 hours from September to October of 2023, capturing 76 tonnes of CO (tCO ) 2 2 over that period. ION achieved capture rates as high as 89% with MEA, where foaming of the MEA prevented operation at higher capture efficiencies. Due to solvent stability issues and the inherently corrosive nature of MEA, ION quickly transitioned to operating with ICE-21™ to safeguard the capital investment of the ENTP project. The MEA campaign was followed by parametric and long-term testing using ION’s proprietary ICE- 21™ capture solvent. The objective of the ICE-21™ campaign was to create a secondary baseline more relevant to commercially available CO capture technologies. ION performed parametric 2 testing with ICE-21™ over approximately 350 hours of testing from October 2023 to December 2023, followed by over 800 hours of long-term testing from January 2024 to February 2024.
